name: Nintendo 3DS family
summary: Explore 3DS family hardware and the model-and-version-specific routes into boot9strap and Luma3DS across 3DS, 3DS XL, 2DS, New 3DS, New 3DS XL and New 2DS XL.

specs.cpu: ARM11 MPCore at 268 MHz (Old models); New models can also run at 804 MHz for applications flagged for it
specs.memory: 128 MB FCRAM (Old models); 256 MB FCRAM (New models)
specs.storage: SD card slot on 3DS, 3DS XL and 2DS; microSD behind the back plate on New models
specs.display: Top 800×240 with 3D on 3DS, 3DS XL, New 3DS and New 3DS XL; bottom 320×240 touchscreen
specs.media: Nintendo 3DS game cards and Nintendo DS game cards

variants.storage: SD card slot; a 2 GB card shipped in the box, SDHC supported
variants.notes: CTR-001. Original clamshell with a 3D top screen and CPU CTR. The guide treats it as an Old model, so the latest version routes to MSET9.

specs.display: 3.53 in 800×240 top screen with 3D; 3.00 in 320×240 bottom screen

variants.notes: SPR-001. Larger screens in the same body class and CPU CTR A; same homebrew endpoint and Old-model entry rules as the 3DS.

specs.display: 4.88 in 800×240 top screen with 3D; 4.18 in 320×240 bottom screen

variants.notes: FTR-001. Fixed slate body, no 3D and a mono speaker; CPU CTR B. Old-model rules apply, and safe mode plus the sleep switch make it the easiest console for the ntrboot route.

specs.display: 3.53 in 800×240 top screen without 3D; 3.00 in 320×240 bottom screen

variants.storage: microSD card behind the back plate
variants.notes: KTR-001. CPU LGR A, 256 MB FCRAM, C-stick, NFC and face-tracking 3D. New-model rules apply; on 11.15.0 and newer the guide uses super-skaterhax instead of MSET9.

specs.cpu: ARM11 MPCore at 268 MHz, up to 804 MHz for flagged applications
specs.display: 3.88 in 800×240 top screen with 3D; 3.33 in 320×240 bottom screen

variants.notes: RED-001. Same New-model hardware in the XL body; the microSD sits behind the back plate, so plan the card swap before starting.

specs.cpu: ARM11 MPCore at 268 MHz, up to 804 MHz for flagged applications
specs.display: 4.88 in 800×240 top screen with 3D; 4.18 in 320×240 bottom screen

variants.storage: microSD card behind the back plate
variants.notes: JAN-001. New-model hardware without 3D; it takes the same entry methods as the New 3DS and New 3DS XL, and its screen size is not stated by the hardware reference used here.

homebrew.name: MSET9
homebrew.firmware: 11.4.0 through 11.17.0; upstream says any region ("probably, haven't tested them all"). Checked 2026-10-28: https://github.com/zoogie/MSET9
homebrew.summary: Starts boot9strap from a prepared SD card through a System Settings flaw, with no game and no extra hardware. The guide sends Old 3DS, Old 3DS XL and Old 2DS consoles on 11.17.0-50 here.

compatibility.note: Upstream says "3ds 11.4-11.17, any region (probably, haven't tested them all)"; this is any-region guidance, not a region-by-region verified compatibility claim. Checked 2026-10-28: https://github.com/zoogie/MSET9

requirements: System version 11.4.0 through 11.17.0.
A Windows, macOS, Linux or SteamOS computer, an Android/ChromeOS device, or an iPhone/iPad that can write to the SD card and run the MSET9 installer.
A full copy of the SD card's contents: the setup hides existing user data until the page is complete.
warnings: The exploit writes to NAND during the boot9strap install; completing the guide's cleanup matters, or installed titles and System Settings can start to misbehave.
An Android phone used as an SD card adapter through MTP does not work; the guide sends that case to its Play Store page.

homebrew.name: super-skaterhax
homebrew.firmware: New models on 11.15.0 through 11.17.0, all regions per the guide text and upstream; the guide's files are published per region (USA, EUR, JPN, KOR)
homebrew.summary: A browser exploit that starts the Homebrew Launcher on New-model consoles on the latest versions. It is known to be unreliable and may need several attempts before it takes.

compatibility.note: The page states New models on version 11.15.0 and above in all regions, then notes the exploit is inconsistent. Upstream lists 11.15-11.17 for all four New-model regions (US, EU, JP, KR); the release files are region-specific.

requirements: A New Nintendo 3DS, New Nintendo 3DS XL or New Nintendo 2DS XL.
System version 11.15.0 through 11.17.0.
The region-specific files for the console's region (USA, EUR, JPN or KOR).
An SD card, a device that can write to it, and temporary region plus date/time changes on the console.
warnings: The guide calls the exploit inconsistent and says to retry up to ten times, then switch to MSET9.
If an Old 3DS reaches this page it only shows the word "Text": that console needs MSET9 instead.

homebrew.name: SSLoth-Browser
homebrew.firmware: 11.4.0 through 11.13.0; the guide routes USA, EUR and KOR, and records the JPN browser path as broken
homebrew.summary: Bypasses the browser's version check so an older browser exploit can run, then loads universal-otherapp. It covers the versions between Soundhax and safecerthax for consoles whose browser is still usable.

compatibility.note: The page states SSLoth lets users on 11.13.0 and below bypass the browser check for new-browserhax or old-browserhax, compatible with 11.4.0 through 11.13.0 in all regions. The guide's picker only routes versions with a matching NVer and marks JPN broken as of 2026-04; the guide routes these versions to MSET9.

requirements: System version 11.4.0 through 11.13.0 with the NVer the guide's table lists for the region.
A working Internet Browser on the console.
SD card, a computer, universal-otherapp and the browser payloads the guide links.
warnings: The route depends on the console's region and exact NVer; a mismatch sends the browser check back and the exploit fails.
The same versions can be done with MSET9, which is not region-limited in the guide.

homebrew.name: safecerthax
homebrew.firmware: 1.0.0 through 11.14.0, all regions, Old models only
homebrew.summary: Uses the console's safe mode and a prepared SD card to install boot9strap on Old 3DS and 2DS consoles up to 11.14.0. The guide checks the shoulder buttons first because the method needs the camera shortcut.

compatibility.note: The page states safecerthax works on all Old 3DS and Old 2DS consoles in all regions from 1.0.0 through 11.14.0 and explicitly does not work on New models.

requirements: An Old Nintendo 3DS, 3DS XL or 2DS.
System version 1.0.0 through 11.14.0.
Working shoulder buttons: the guide opens the camera with L+R first and stops if it does not appear.
SD card and a computer.
warnings: A console whose L+R camera shortcut does not work cannot use this method; the guide sends it to MSET9.

homebrew.name: Soundhax
homebrew.summary: Plays a crafted audio file in the 3DS Sound app to launch universal-otherapp. It is the original route and still the documented one for consoles that never went past 11.3.0.

compatibility.note: The page states Soundhax with universal-otherapp is compatible with versions 1.0.0 through 11.3.0 in all regions.

requirements: System version 1.0.0 through 11.3.0.
The Soundhax .m4a file for the console's region, model and version.
SD card, a computer and universal-otherapp.
warnings: The audio file is built per region, model and version; a mismatched file does not launch.

homebrew.name: ntrboot
homebrew.firmware: Every system version; needs a compatible DS flashcart
homebrew.summary: Boots a recovery-mode cartridge before the console's system software loads, so it installs boot9strap on any version and also recovers a console that no longer starts. It is the hardware fallback for the whole family.

compatibility.note: The page describes ntrboot as working on all 3DS family consoles because it runs before any other part of the operating system. It needs an ntrboot-compatible DS flashcart and a magnet, except on the Old 2DS, which uses its sleep switch.

requirements: A compatible DS flashcart flashed with ntrboot.
A magnet strong enough to put the console into sleep mode (the Old 2DS uses its sleep switch instead).
SD card with the SafeB9SInstaller and boot9strap files.
warnings: The guide recommends having the flashcart and magnet ready before you need them, because ntrboot is also the recovery route for a console that no longer boots.

homebrew.name: Hardmod (boot9strap install)
homebrew.firmware: Every system version that has a matching FIRM file; requires soldering
homebrew.summary: Dumps the NAND through a soldered connection, installs boot9strap into the image and writes it back. It is the last resort for a console that cannot boot and for versions with no software route.

compatibility.note: The page states this works on New 3DS, New 2DS, Old 3DS and Old 2DS on all versions that have a corresponding .firm file, and it builds on the FIRM partitions known-plaintext exploit.

requirements: A soldered NAND access (hardmod) and a NAND dump from it.
The .firm file matching the console model and system version.
hardmod-b9s-installer on Windows, macOS or Linux.
warnings: Soldering and a full NAND dump are required; a mistake here can make the console unrecoverable.
Keep the untouched NAND dump: it is the only way back if the modified image fails.

homebrew.name: Luma3DS
homebrew.firmware: Every system version; requires boot9strap and is not itself an entry point
homebrew.summary: The custom firmware that patches the 3DS at boot, after boot9strap has been installed. It also provides the Select-at-boot configuration menu and the region-free behaviour the guide relies on.

compatibility.note: Luma3DS loads from boot9strap before the system menu, so it is not tied to one system version; the version list here is the family's supported system versions, not a per-release matrix. v13.4 is the current release.

requirements: boot9strap already installed through one of the entry methods.
The current Luma3DS files copied to the SD card root.
warnings: Do not install a second CFW or loader over boot9strap; the guide's CFW check exists to catch that case.
A system update does not remove boot9strap once installed, but the initial install still needs a version-appropriate entry.

homebrew.name: GodMode9
homebrew.firmware: Requires boot9strap or Luma3DS; not firmware-specific
homebrew.summary: The file manager the guide uses for NAND and save backups, title dumps and the CTRTransfer procedure. It runs with system-level access, so it can change things a normal app cannot.

compatibility.note: Loads from boot9strap or Luma3DS on any installed system version; it is not an entry point and has no firmware list of its own.

requirements: A console with boot9strap installed.
The GodMode9 files on the SD card.
warnings: Use it for backups and dumps; writing system titles casually can brick the console.

homebrew.name: Universal-Updater
homebrew.firmware: Requires Luma3DS; no firmware list of its own
homebrew.summary: A homebrew app store that runs on the console and installs other homebrew over Wi-Fi. The guide says homebrew internet access still works after the Nintendo Network shutdown.

compatibility.note: Runs on any console with the guide's Luma3DS setup; its own project does not publish a system-version matrix.

requirements: A console with Luma3DS set up.
Wi-Fi access on the console.
warnings: Installing homebrew is the same trust decision as on any platform; check the source before installing.

homebrew.name: Nintendo 3DS system update
homebrew.summary: Nintendo's own update path for a 3DS that still boots, including Recovery Mode (L+R+Up+A at power-on). It installs the current release only and is not a route back to an older version.

compatibility.note: Nintendo's update page lists 11.17.0-50 as the newest 3DS system software; the official path installs the current release, not a version chosen by the user.

requirements: A console that still reaches the HOME Menu or Recovery Mode (L+R+Up+A at power-on).
Internet access, or Nintendo's documented update method.
warnings: The update path cannot install an older version; it is not a downgrade route.
Do not update in the middle of a homebrew setup; finish the guide's steps first.

homebrew.name: CTRTransfer
homebrew.firmware: Installs an 11.15.0 image; requires boot9strap and Luma3DS first
homebrew.summary: Writes an 11.15.0 system image for the console's model and region with GodMode9, then reinstalls tickets. The guide documents it as an add-on repair step for a console that already has custom firmware.

compatibility.note: The page installs an 11.15.0 CTRTransfer image and assumes Luma3DS and boot9strap are already installed; it does not publish a per-version support list.

requirements: boot9strap and Luma3DS already installed.
GodMode9, FBI, faketik, ctrtransfer.gm9 and the 11.15.0 image for the console's model and region.
A NAND backup taken before the transfer.
warnings: The transfer resets system settings (username, country, language); installed games and their saves are kept.
CTRTransfer images are distributed by torrent; verify what you download.
This is a repair step, not a supported way to pick an older system version.

homebrew.name: 3DS firmware rollback status — no verified general method
homebrew.firmware: No general rollback method documented; Nintendo ships updates forward-only
homebrew.summary: Records the documented 3DS limit: Nintendo's update page offers only the current release, so an older system version is not an official option. NAND restores and CTRTransfer are repair paths for one console, not a version selector.

compatibility.note: No model-specific rollback method was verified; the official update page lists only the newest release.

warnings: A NAND backup restored through GodMode9 or ntrboot belongs to that console; it is recovery, not a version selector.
CTRTransfer installs an 11.15.0 image and is documented as a repair/add-on, not as a general downgrade.
